items.summary: A Smashing Magazine exploration of the native CSS random() function, now shipped in Safari and rolling out in Chrome 156, with CodePen demos for organic typography, bouncing letters, splayed cards, and a punk fanzine.
items.title: Embracing Playful Imperfection With The CSS `random()` Function

items.summary: axuse is an accessibility-first browser and computer-use MCP server for agent harnesses (Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode). It instruments the DOM, accessibility tree and CDP instead of using a screenshot loop, has zero npm dependencies and needs Node 22+.
items.title: ctoldigital/axuse

items.summary: DeepInfer is an open-source high-performance inference framework for DeepSeek models, used in DeepSeek's production services. It offers offline inference with optimized kernels, MoE parallelism, speculative decoding, batch-invariant inference, deterministic sampling and structured outputs.
items.title: DeepInfer: High-performance inference framework for DeepSeek models

items.summary: EAGLE-4 is a speculative decoding drafter for accelerating LLM inference that adapts its strategy to batch size, hardware and workload. The eagle-harness pip package serves EAGLE-4 drafts on SGLang, vLLM and TokenSpeed via engine hooks.
items.title: eagle-hq/EAGLE-4

items.summary: A WhatsApp MCP server that runs in your own Cloudflare account lets an AI agent search and read your WhatsApp chats. It links once as a device, stores messages in a SQLite Durable Object and cannot send messages.
items.title: Show HN: WhatsApp MCP running free on Cloudflare

items.summary: ra-jit is a Rust JIT toolchain that applies live code edits to an already-running program in about a millisecond while preserving state, plus faster incremental builds via `cargo ra-jit build|run|test|check`. Benchmarks on ripgrep, nushell and others show builds 3–20x faster than incremental cargo.
items.title: indexable-inc/ra-jit

items.summary: tsrs is a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler, built by Cloudflare and VoidZero with Owner.com's Max Schwenk inside the Oxc toolchain rather than as a fork. Early benchmarks claim up to 8x speedups and ~70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0, with some optimizations upstreamed.
items.title: Tsrs: A Port of TypeScript to Rust

items.summary: Stackyard is a free open-source Windows/macOS app that inventories every SDK, toolchain and framework version on a machine, shows which projects use each, flags what is safe to remove, and fixes problems in one click. It also offers a marketplace of publisher-sourced SDK installs with hash verification.
items.title: AqibJavedZeepalm/stackyard

items.summary: Josh Comeau's blog post on upcoming CSS features, walking through his top 10 votes for Interop 2027, starting with the proposed @function rule for defining reusable CSS functions. Includes tips usable today.
items.title: The Future of CSS

items.summary: A FlowingData chart post on 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances data showing net worth percentiles by age group, with a table of median, 90th and 99th percentile figures per age bracket.
items.title: Rising to higher net worth, by age

items.summary: Sumi.css, a minimalist classless-first CSS framework: one 6.7 KB file, no build step, no JS or dependencies. Styles headings, forms, tables, cards, accordions, modals and nav from plain semantic HTML, with light/dark mode, custom-property theming, zero-specificity overrides and ARIA-driven states.
items.title: Show HN: Sumi.css – CSS Framework

items.summary: MyAgent is a Python general-purpose Agent Runtime repo built around a harness that handles permissions, tool execution, context compression, long-term memory, SKILL.md-based skills with self-evolution, an MCP stdio client, and sub-agents, supporting both OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs.
items.title: ztt0216/MyAgent

items.summary: Omnara is an open-source, self-hostable managed agent platform (Apache 2.0) positioned as an alternative to Claude Managed Agents and OpenAI's Agents API, running agents on any model and machine with tools, secrets, permissions and streaming; agents are launched via agent.yaml, a Node CLI, or a TypeScript SDK.
items.title: Show HN: Omnara – Open-source alternative to Claude Managed Agents

items.summary: Antirion is an open-source AI gateway shipped as a single Rust binary with a built-in admin console, routing requests across many model providers with fallback chains, cost budgets, guardrails, caching and MCP/agent gateways, claiming lower overhead and higher throughput than Bifrost and LiteLLM.
items.title: eliasbiondo/antirion

items.summary: MemT-1.0 is a family of memory foundation models (Nano and Flash) that make persistent, dynamically evolving memory part of model computation via local and hyper memory blocks with Mixture-of-Storage, cutting storage roughly 66x versus full-context KV cache at 128K history and ranking first and second on 11 memory benchmarks.
items.title: MemTensor/MemT-1.0

items.summary: Claude Super Sidebar is a plugin giving a native Claude Code pane plus a read-only local Codex session dashboard that shows main agent/subagent relationships, execution status and task steps in one panel, with no frontend build. Its docs flag that current native engine validation and latest isolation regressions remain unverified.
items.title: Zafer-Liu/claude-super-sidebar

items.summary: stalemap is an npm tool that finds dependencies whose APIs changed after a coding model's training cutoff and informs the agent via AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md notes, a type-check guard after each edit, and a search_changes MCP tool. In a pre-registered blind benchmark of 66 tasks, agents passed 89% of sessions versus 68% with no help.
items.title: Umair/stalemap

items.summary: LayerFS is a filesystem for AI coding agents where each tool call is a commit on a branch, forks are zero-cost metadata copies, same-file clashes are refused, and every line records the step that wrote it. It also keeps ignored files and claims ~0.05s mounts versus ~5 min reinstall.
items.title: LayerFS: The filesystem for AI coding agents

items.summary: A data analysis of movie shot counts from 1920 through 2025, showing a long-term increase and recent plateau, based on TransNet V2 transition detection and shot counting.
items.title: Increasing number of shots in movies

items.summary: An interactive data story on the “Six Degrees of Kevin Bacon” that calculates actor remoteness and finds Samuel L. Jackson, not Kevin Bacon, is Hollywood’s most central actor, with women underrepresented in the top 100.
items.title: The Real Kevin Bacon

items.summary: A blog article on building an isolated preview for AI-generated HTML, starting from the naive iframe srcdoc approach, breaking it three ways, then rebuilding it to show tested protections and their limits.
items.title: Building an Isolated Preview for AI-Generated HTML

items.summary: OpenShell, a runtime that sandboxes fleets of autonomous AI agents, enforcing per-agent policy on file access, syscalls and network via kernel instrumentation and formally verifying policy changes before approval. 0.1.x adds a stable release cadence, new isolation primitives, an expanded extension surface and new APIs.
items.title: OpenShell – A safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents

items.summary: A blog post arguing that asking an LLM for a confidence score or probability produces a number with no good reason to be trusted, illustrated by comparing machine confidence to a weather forecaster's, whose certainty is a calculation over information, not an opinion.
items.title: Using LLM for confidence scoring is a bad idea

items.summary: Lampline, a local-first platform that imports Dialogflow CX and CX Agent Studio agents and runs them on your own hardware, with a drag-and-drop builder mixing LLM and scripted steps, test console, HTTP/MCP tools and phone calls via Twilio, Telnyx or SIP, at roughly $0.02–0.17 a call.
items.title: C4rohan/Lampline

items.summary: DecisionPivot (formerly DecideBench), a benchmark and code repo for evaluating decision models that output option probabilities at LLM system control points, measuring correctness, robustness to one decisive detail changing, and how much work a model handles at a fixed error rate.
items.title: StartLuxLabs/DecisionPivot

items.summary: A dbos.dev blog post on making Postgres DELETE scale, explaining MVCC delete costs and tuning cache/index performance in a Postgres-backed durable workflows and queues workload to apply retention policies at tens of thousands of workflows and steps per second.
items.title: How Postgres DELETE can actually scale

items.summary: A GitHub-hosted OpenAI CLI for calling the OpenAI REST API from a terminal or shell scripts, with commands to generate images, upload/download files, submit and wait on batches, list models, and format output as JSON/JSONL; it also distinguishes itself from Codex CLI.
items.title: OpenAI CLI

items.summary: A yoyo-code.com blog post on why 2026 is an exciting year for the Rust compiler, covering the next-generation trait solver, the Polonius borrow checker, and compiler-performance work as long-term initiatives reach final steps.
items.title: 2026 is an exciting year for the Rust compiler (and me)

items.summary: Chrome's experimental HTML-in-Canvas API, now in origin trial, lets developers draw DOM content into a 2D canvas or WebGL/WebGPU texture while keeping the UI interactive and accessible, avoiding the usual DOM-versus-canvas tradeoff.
items.title: The HTML-in-Canvas API origin trial

items.summary: Safari Technology Preview 255 release notes list WebKit fixes across accessibility, animations, and CSS, including corrected getComputedStyle() pseudo-element animation checks, view transition update callback flushing, and font-family: initial resolution.
items.title: Release Notes for Safari Technology Preview 255

items.summary: A blog post recounts a side project that hosted HTML files in an afternoon and, eight months later, drew as many weekly users as the company’s $150k Looker licence, with Looker usage down a third.
items.title: Can we replace a $150k Looker with a bucket of HTML files?

items.summary: Five-layer 2026 AI engineering roadmap built around RAG, agents and evals, each layer ending in a showable mini-project, plus a 12-week sample plan (~25 weeks at 10 hrs/week); it argues evaluation engineering is the skill to learn first.
items.title: h9-tec/ai-roadmap-2026

items.summary: Source-backed catalog of papers, models, datasets, benchmarks and tools for computer-use agents, with an English survey manuscript, topic browsing, a coverage ledger and scheduled discovery scans three times daily.
items.title: reacher-z/Awesome-CUA

items.summary: Community plugin adding blackboard blocks to PTC mode in DeepSeek Harness so the model decides what to compact, closing a block with a handover summary; v0.4.0 uses block_compact({ids, content}) and drops block_summary.
items.title: mengwEX/dsh-block-ptc

items.summary: OpenAI-compatible proxy for the Gemini web app that authenticates with Google session cookies instead of an API key, adding account pooling, quota-aware failover, image/video generation, Search grounding and a built-in MCP server.
items.title: azrinaldi/gemini-stealth-bridge

items.summary: Corgi is a terminal multiplexer for humans and agents that shows each agent's status, token activity and file changes, keeps processes running in the background like tmux, and adds agent-aware tabs, worktrees, resource usage and image paste.
items.title: Show HN: Corgi, a helpful {agent, terminal} multiplexer

items.summary: Vesalius gives Claude Code a locally built map of a repository so it can answer code questions with exact file and line references in fewer calls; its benchmark cut token use roughly in half and it also ships as a Mac app and VS Code extension.
items.title: haplollc/Vesalius

items.summary: OpenIDEA is an IntelliJ IDEA-style IDE rebuilt in Rust, offering editor, code insight, debugger, Git, terminal, database and HTTP clients for 60+ languages on macOS, Windows and Linux, with benchmarks showing faster startup and lower memory than IntelliJ IDEA.
items.title: l0ng-ai/openidea

items.summary: Dominik’s “Vertical Codebase” architecture idea proposes co-locating hooks, types, queries, and other related files by conceptual site areas such as the dashboard, extending component-level co-location instead of spreading them out.
items.title: The Vertical Codebase

items.summary: An article on accordion icon UX research finding the caret is the safest icon choice, split menus and split buttons are harmful, and icon/text labels should not link to different actions; no icon implies a direct page link.
items.title: Accordion Icons: Which Work Best?

items.summary: The Browser Company's farewell to Arc: new accounts stop Oct 22, mobile AI features end Nov 23, and Arc on macOS/Windows shuts down Dec 22, with data importing into successor browser Dia, which the team now focuses on for security.
items.title: A farewell to Arc browser

items.summary: A fork of llama.cpp that steers any of 131 supported architectures away from refusals at inference time by reading comply/refuse directions from the prompt itself, leaving weights untouched. Reports refusal on Qwen3-8B dropping from 96.3% to 7.9% on held-out harmful prompts and 82% to 0% on JailbreakBench, with no training or extra files.
items.title: heterodoxin/AbliteratedOutTheBox

items.summary: Alter (YC S25) is a privileged access management layer for AI agents: per-agent identities and scoped grants, a vault that injects credentials per request, default-deny and human-approval policy, and a tamper-evident audit trail. One SDK call handles storage, refresh, policy and audit across 140 providers, with LangChain, MCP and AWS integrations.
items.title: Launch HN: Alter (YC S25) – Access control for multi-user agents

items.summary: A video titled “RuneScape Bench: MMOs for Agents,” with a related link to the LostCityRS Server repository.
items.title: RuneScape Bench: MMOs for Agents [video]

items.summary: bili-cli (PyPI package bili-agent) is a CLI giving AI agents 80+ commands and 17 MCP tools to run a Bilibili account as a creator: replying to comments and DMs, watching videos with transcripts and frame overviews, and posting videos and dynamics. It auto-installs its skills into 18 agents and ships default safety guardrails.
items.title: kukemc/bili-cli

items.summary: blaze is a Rust build engine that runs alongside Cargo and recompiles only changed functions into an already-built program, claiming 10–24× faster edit rebuilds on real projects; opt-in programs can take new code while running.
items.title: indexable-inc/blaze

items.summary: HatchZip is a free open-source archive extractor with desktop and CLI apps that extracts ZIP, 7z, RAR, tar and split archives in place, consuming the archive as it goes so only output space is needed; it checks fit, keeps a margin, and resumes after interruption.
items.title: xevrion/hatchzip

items.summary: A first-person history of rqlite and the distributed-SQLite category from 2014 onward, arguing rqlite was the first open-source system to combine Raft and SQLite and tracing its design choices and later projects.
items.title: Twelve years of distributed SQLite

items.summary: An Agent Skills kit for converting WordPress sites to static Astro with a coding agent, preserving URLs, content, SEO metadata, media paths, redirects and responsive design via exact Node scripts and gates, ending in a pull request and staging deploy.
items.title: ethanplusai/astro-conversion-kit

items.summary: A skill that teaches coding agents senior product-designer taste for analytics, revenue and metrics dashboards on web or SwiftUI, covering KPI tiles, charts, filters, empty states and layouts, with screenshot QA; distilled from 127 shipped screens and a real redesign.
items.title: abdiraimov-otabek/dashboard-design-skill

items.summary: Bloffy is a privacy-first blogging platform for Markdown and raw HTML that adds only a 3.2KB script, offers split-view editing, custom domains, CSS themes, multilingual posts, IndexNow, and team members; its Show HN claim is a 99 PageSpeed score and near-100 PSI targets.
items.title: Show HN: I built a Markdown and raw HTML blog platform scoring 99 on PageSpeed

items.summary: Chaos is a function-based programming language that treats agents as callable values, so precise computation lives in functions while understanding and generation go to agents. It ships with a web IDE, runtime graph, and page/report artifacts, and demos run without model keys.
items.title: Cattmonkey/ChaosIntelligence

items.summary: PaperPilot is a Rust PDF toolkit available as an MCP server, CLI, WASM browser tool, Tauri desktop app, and local REST API, so files are processed locally with no cloud calls. Features include merge, split, rotate, OCR, compress, PII scan, and sanitize.
items.title: PaperPilot – Zero-Cloud, Pure-Rust PDF Engine with WASM and MCP

items.summary: Microsoft-Decision-1, built on Alibaba's Qwen3.5-9B, scores a fixed list of answer options in a single forward pass and returns a calibrated probability for each instead of generating text. It targets routing, classification, prioritization, and verification, via Microsoft Foundry and OpenRouter.
items.title: Microsoft Decision-1: 9B Qwen Model Launch Explained

items.summary: An essay on agentic monitoring, citing Anthropic's use of "superfan" Claudes—one per system component, with telemetry and log access—to catch subtle, novel issues that traditional alerts miss as systems grow too large for humans to watch closely.
items.title: Agentic Monitoring

items.summary: Farol, a free open-source CLI and GitHub Action, tells the person approving a pull request how risky the merge is and which files carry the risk, using static analysis after AI review.
items.title: Show HN: Farol – A risk map of a pull request for the person who approves it

items.summary: openide is a free, open-source IDE built on Material Design 3 and Monaco Editor that generates HCT tonal palettes and matching syntax themes from any seed color, with hot-reloaded configs, plugins, and themes plus an integrated code runner.
items.title: AbdulSamad350z/openide

items.summary: Pilot is a Python tool that turns labeled tickets from GitHub, Linear, Jira, or Asana into reviewed pull requests by planning, coding, testing, linting, and opening a PR linked to the issue, with configurable autopilot modes.
items.title: peterhoang1103991-cmd/pilot-ai-ticket-shipper

items.summary: Reports that Chrome can send copied content to Google's servers for scanning for unsafe material.
items.title: Google's servers can scan what you copy in Chrome for unsafe content

items.summary: First part of a two-part post introducing TanStack AI, a strongly typed ecosystem of AI libraries for adding AI features to apps, covering setup, AI requests, streaming, persistence and resumability, with code samples in a repo.
items.title: Unlocking AI in Your Apps with TanStack AI

items.summary: WebKit's Safari 27.2 feature update refines Customizable Select with a new ::field-content pseudo-element, adjusted UA styles and safe alignment so the picker stays in view, renames a Grid Lanes property, and includes 20 bug fixes.
items.title: WebKit Features for Safari 27.2

items.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra is a fast, low-cost model for visual reasoning and precise computer use. Its standard API prices are 50% below GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol, and it completes agentic tasks over three times faster than GPT-6 Astra and Sol.
items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra

items.summary: A blog post on fixing tool-call schema accuracy when serving open-weight models like Kimi K2.6 with vLLM, which produced valid tool-call schemas only 92% of the time. It explains how constrained decoding, released as a server-side flag in vLLM 0.31, restores 100% schema accuracy.
items.title: Fixing Tool-Call Accuracy in vLLM

items.summary: OpenAI's developer model page for GPT-6.1 Terra, a fast, efficient model for visual reasoning, precise computer use, and natural writing, priced at $1 input/$5 output per 1M tokens with a 1,050,000-token context window; tool calling requires the Responses API.
items.title: GPT 6.1 Terra

items.summary: Hob (FrigadeHQ/hob) is a free, open-source, offline desktop app that runs open-weight models like Gemma and gpt-oss locally on Mac, Windows and Linux, positioned as an alternative to Claude and ChatGPT. It auto-selects the best frontier open-weight model that fits your computer and sets it up.
items.title: Show HN: Hob - Open-source, on device alternative to Claude Cowork and ChatGPT

items.summary: globalmpc/nomore is a GitHub repo offering 20 ready-made CLAUDE.md rules distilled from nearly 10,000 Claude Code issues, plus an npx tool that finds instructions you keep repeating. Each rule links to the issue and reactions behind it.
items.title: globalmpc/nomore

items.summary: Entire is a new Git forge built for agent-human collaboration, with three primitives: Trails (agent-scored automated evals on every push instead of diff-based PR review), distributed Git hosting claimed up to 89x faster than GitHub, and Continuous Memory syncing sessions and prompts into the repo.
items.title: The Git Forge for Agent-Human Collaboration

items.summary: Pragtical v3.14.0 is a release of the Lua-based text editor adding application menus and a movable toolbar, command prompts that can float or sit top/center, workspace session management, a refreshed Plugin Manager, and lower idle CPU use.
items.title: Pragtical v3.14 Lua-based text editor adds menus, floating views, and sessions

items.summary: A guide to dynamic social media card images for user-generated or e-commerce pages, covering how to generate them from dynamic data and expose them via Open Graph and Twitter meta tags, with GitHub as an example.
items.title: What should you put on a dynamic custom social media card image?

items.summary: A Halloween whodunit-style article tracing why Extended Validation certificates lost their green address-bar prominence, naming browsers, humans, a nonprofit, and Stripe as suspects, and noting a possible revival via an EU standard and AI agents.
items.title: Who killed the EV cert? A browser whodunit for Halloween
